title: Developments on Fair Consideration Framework and Measures on Discriminatory Hiring Practices
what_it_is: Developments on Fair Consideration Framework and Measures on Discriminatory Hiring Practices

sections.label: Questions on Fair Consideration Framework
sections.summary: Questions ask whether errant companies on the FCF watchlist will be named, whether any were removed, and for an update on tripartite fair employment discussions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower in light of more companies being put on the Fair Consideration Framework watchlist, whether the Ministry will consider naming the errant companies to serve as a deterrent to others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) whether the Ministry will name the companies that have been placed on the Fair Consideration Framework (FCF) watchlist for potentially discriminatory hiring practices; (b) whether any of the companies previously placed on FCF watchlist have been removed from the watchlist; and (c) if so, what are the criteria used.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower whether she can provide an update on the latest tripartite discussions relating to fair employment practices, in particular discriminatory hiring and human resource practices, including nationality, race, age and religious-based discrimination.

sections.label: Work pass suspensions for FCF infringements
sections.summary: MOM has taken employers to task, and this year 90 employers had work pass privileges suspended for FCF infringements including age and gender discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For example, MOM has regularly taken employers to task for pre-selecting a foreign candidate and disregarding qualified local candidates.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This year alone, 90 employers have had their work pass privileges suspended because of infringements under the Fair Consideration Framework or FCF, including for age and gender discrimination.

sections.label: About 400 firms on FCF Watchlist
sections.summary: About 400 firms are on the FCF Watchlist for a higher share of foreign PMETs than industry peers or high concentrations of a single foreign nationality source.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: To questions by Mr Louis Chua and Mr Seah Kian Peng, there are currently about 400 firms placed on the FCF Watchlist for having a higher share of foreign PMETs compared to their industry peers, or high concentrations of a single foreign nationality source.

sections.label: FCF scrutiny and local PMET hires
sections.summary: Since 2016 more than 1,200 employers were scrutinised under the FCF, and watchlist firms hired more than 4,800 Singaporean PMETs in total.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Since 2016, more than 1,200 employers have been scrutinised under the FCF.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: On the other hand, firms on the FCF Watchlist have hired more than 4,800 Singaporean PMETs in total.

sections.label: Employers reviewing cost-saving measures
sections.summary: Of the 850 employers engaged, close to 40% reviewed their cost-saving measures to give more wage support to their employees.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Of the 850 employers engaged, close to 40% reviewed their cost-saving measures to give more wage support to their employees.

sections.label: Retrenchment notification requirement
sections.summary: MOM requires employers with 10 or more employees that retrenched at least five employees within any six-month period to submit a retrenchment notification, covering close to 90% of the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In addition, MOM requires employers with 10 or more employees that have retrenched at least five employees within any six-month period to submit a retrenchment notification.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This covers close to 90% of the workforce in Singapore.

sections.label: Notification expansion for SMEs
sections.summary: The Government is mindful not to impose excessive reporting requirements on SMEs and micro-SMEs where effort may not match impact.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: To Mr Patrick Tay’s suggestion to expand the notification to more employers, we are mindful not to impose excessive reporting requirements on SMEs and micro-SMEs where the effort may not be commensurate with impact.

sections.label: FCF Watchlist company count
sections.summary: The speaker notes she mentioned there are 1,200 companies on the FCF Watchlist.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, I think she mentioned there are 1,200 companies on the FCF Watchlist.

sections.label: Penalties for discrimination against women
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether guidelines against discrimination against women and mothers can be legislated with penalties as deterrence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But if you discriminate against women and mothers, and the penalty is that you cannot hire foreigners, then I hope the Minister agrees with me that that does not really make sense.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: So, the question is whether we can legislate these guidelines, have proper penalties in place that will serve as a better deterrence against discrimination against women and mothers.

sections.label: Government openness to legislation
sections.summary: The Government is not averse to using legislation provided it can achieve a good effect.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: First, the Government is not so averse to using legislation, provided it can achieve a good effect.

sections.label: Keeping options open
sections.summary: The speaker tells Mr Louis Ng the Government keeps options open but must ask what the crux is.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: And I had texted him to say that this is not unthinkable, it is something that we can discuss, whether we want to move forward.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, my answer to Mr Louis Ng is, yes, we always keep the options open, but we must ask ourselves what is the crux here.

sections.label: Surveillance did not pick them up
sections.summary: The answer is no, not due to special concession or treatment, but because proactive surveillance did not pick them up.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The answer is no, not because they were given any special concession or treatment, but the proactive surveillance that we carried out did not pick them up.

sections.label: Companies not yet exited
sections.summary: The number of companies that have not yet exited is in the minority, put at less than 10%.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The last question is on how many companies that have not yet exited.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: They are in the minority; I will put it at less than 10%.

sections.label: Watchlist firm types and reporting
sections.summary: It asks the proportion of MNCs, LLEs, SMEs and micro-SMEs among 400 watchlist firms, and notes concern over MOM not requiring SME reporting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The other one is, among these 400 firms that are on the watchlist, what proportion are MNCs, what are LLEs, SMEs and micro-SMEs?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: On the mandatory retrenchment reporting, I am a bit concerned that MOM is taking the position that we do not require micro-SMEs and SMEs to do mandatory reporting.

sections.label: Worker complaints and investigations
sections.summary: It does not prevent the worker from raising the issue with MOM, and MOM also investigated many cases where individuals complained.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: It does not prevent the worker himself from raising the issue with MOM.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I mentioned that apart from those that we have investigated after they submitted the mandatory retrenchment notification, on top of that, we also investigated an even larger number of those where individuals complained to us.

sections.label: Companies exiting Singapore
sections.summary: In some instances companies decided they could not meet the requirements and decided to exit Singapore altogether.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Naming them or continuing to suspend their work pass privileges?

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I can share with Mr Tay that in some instances, the companies have decided that it is not possible for them to meet up to these requirements and they have decided to exit Singapore altogether.

sections.label: Curtailed work pass privileges
sections.summary: Naming them or not would not have made much difference, but curtailing their work pass privileges made the difference.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Whether you name them or not would not have made much of a difference.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: But the fact that you have curtailed their work pass privileges, that is what has really made the difference.

sections.label: Mystery Shopper methodology question
sections.summary: It asks whether the Ministry has used or is considering using the Mystery Shopper methodology to look for companies with discriminatory hiring practices.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The third question, Mr Speaker, is to ask, whether or not, the Ministry has used or is considering using the "Mystery Shopper" methodology to look for companies with discriminatory hiring practices.

sections.label: EP and S Pass applications review
sections.summary: The Government will evaluate EP and S Pass applications based on companies' support for local PMETs, including retrenchment behaviour and responsiveness to recruitment and training efforts.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We will continue to look at better ways of identifying companies, more that can be picked up accurately, swiftly and at the same time, what further measures will get the companies to reshape their workforce profiles more quickly.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I mentioned on Tuesday that we are evaluating EP and S Pass applications, going to look back at whether the company has kept up its support for local PMETs in their employment.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: That would include their retrenchment behaviour; it will have a bearing.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: That will also include whether they have been responsive to efforts by Government agencies to help them recruit and train local PMETs; that will also have a bearing on their EP and S Pass applications.

sections.label: Balance and MyCareersFuture advertising exemption
sections.summary: Striking the right balance is needed, and jobs with fixed monthly salary of $20,000 or above are exempted from advertising on MyCareersFuture.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: You cannot overly rely on just one and also create an environment where there is so much distrust and no one believes that it is actually important each one does their part, to strengthen the workforce profiles within businesses and striking the right balance is what we must strive to do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: There are jobs with fixed monthly salary of $20,000 or above which are exempted from advertising on the MyCareersFuture.

sections.label: Mystery Shopper and advertising requirement
sections.summary: The $20,000 threshold only concerns advertising, and the Mystery Shopper approach can still identify companies with concerning workforce profiles even if jobs are not advertised.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I should also just add this as an important caveat – we are not depending only on the FCF's advertising requirement.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This question of the $20,000 is only relevant for whether the job is being advertised.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: But, as I explained earlier, even if the job is not advertised, just using the "Mystery Shopper" approach that Dr Tan had advocated, we can still identify companies whose workforce profiles give us cause for concern.
